# Results — Study 765 (Stock-to-Flow)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — PlanB's
**Stock-to-Flow** model (2019): Bitcoin's price obeys a power law in its scarcity,
`ln(price) = a + b·ln(SF)` where `SF = stock / annual-flow`, reported in-sample R² ~ 0.95, with
famous six-figure price predictions. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `74d40e852645` (BTC-USD).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| S2F curve | **reconstructed from the issuance schedule** (consensus law, not a proxy): block reward 50 BTC halving every 210,000 blocks; stock is EXACT at every halving (10.5M / 15.75M / 18.375M / 19.6875M), interpolated linearly by date within each epoch; flow = `reward × 144 blocks/day × 365`. `SF = stock/flow`, doubling at each halving. No network. |
| Real tape | yfinance daily BTC-USD close (4,305 rows), 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-30. Price-only == total-return for BTC (no dividends). |
| SF today | ≈ **122** (stock ≈ 20.05M BTC, flow ≈ 164k BTC/yr after the 2024 halving) |
| Fit | OLS of `ln(price)` on `ln(SF)`. Steelman = full-sample monthly **market-cap** fit (PlanB's own dependent variable); honest test = coefficients **frozen at the publication date 2019-03-22** and projected forward. |
| Execution | valuation residual (price vs the frozen model line) known at day *t*'s close → position held from *t+1* (one-day lag, the study's single documented convention). 10 bps one-way × NAV per switch. |
| Named limitation | within-epoch daily supply is interpolated between exact halving anchors (real block intervals wobble around 10 min); the halving anchors — all that matters for the model's structure — are exact. yfinance BTC-USD begins 2014-09, so our in-sample window is shorter than PlanB's 2009-start fit. |

No survivorship on the Signal axis (BTC-USD is a single-asset price index; its "one surviving
coin" character is a Bitcoin-wide caveat, named on the Tradability axis).

## 1 · The fit that made it famous — and why it flatters

| Fit | dependent var | sample | R² |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Steelman | ln(market cap) ~ ln(SF), monthly | full 2014-09 → 2026-06 (142 mo) | **0.887** |
| Spurious control A | ln(price) ~ ln(SF), daily | full | 0.880 |
| Spurious control B | ln(price) ~ **calendar time**, daily | full | **0.876** |

`corr( ln(SF), time ) = 0.964`. **The S2F fit and a plain price-on-time trend are statistically
indistinguishable** (R² 0.880 vs 0.876). Because `ln(SF)` is a near-deterministic staircase of
the halving schedule — essentially a clock — regressing a trending log-price on it is a textbook
spurious regression of two non-stationary series. The dazzling R² certifies almost nothing about
scarcity: any smoothly rising asset would "fit".

## 2 · Out-of-sample — coefficients frozen at publication (2019-03-22)

Fit only on data that existed at publication (1,648 days), then score the untouched future
(2,657 days). Frozen coefficients `a = -0.871, b = 2.766`.

| | in-sample (→ 2019-03) | out-of-sample (2019-03 →) |
|---|--:|--:|
| R² | **0.705** | **0.213** |
| log RMSE | 0.739 | 0.770 |

| Date | Actual BTC | Model (frozen) | actual / model |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2021-11-30 (cycle top) | $57,005 | $30,857 | 1.85 |
| 2022-11-30 (bottom) | $17,169 | $32,384 | 0.53 |
| 2024-12-31 | $93,429 | $239,071 | 0.39 |
| 2026-06-30 (as-of) | $58,559 | **$247,369** | **0.24** |

The model's R² collapses from 0.71 to 0.21 out-of-sample. It **under**-shot into the 2021 top,
then — as SF doubled at the 2024 halving — its predicted price exploded to a **six-figure floor**
while the realised tape sat ~4× lower. By the as-of date the model is off by a factor of four.

## 3 · Is the valuation residual tradable? (Signal axis)

"Price below the model line" as an undervaluation signal. Overlapping forward BTC returns
regressed on the lagged residual, Newey-West (HAC) *t* at lag 1.5× horizon. A genuine
buy-when-cheap effect needs a **negative** slope clearing |t| ≥ 2.

| horizon | slope | HAC *t* (out-of-sample) | HAC *t* (full sample) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| +30d | −0.015 | −0.62 | −1.48 |
| +90d | −0.121 | −1.51 | −2.50 |
| +180d | −0.435 | **−1.68** | −2.81 |
| +365d | −0.187 | −0.45 | −1.64 |

Out-of-sample, **no horizon clears |t| = 2** (best −1.68 at 180 days). The full-sample columns
*do* cross 2 at 90/180 days — but that is precisely the in-sample fit leaking back in
(the residual is defined relative to a line fit on that same data), not out-of-sample evidence.
The honest, look-ahead-free test finds no certifiable predictive signal.

## 4 · Timer vs buy-and-hold (Tradability axis)

Long BTC whenever the residual is below zero (price cheap vs the frozen model line), cash
otherwise; one-day lag, 10 bps one-way × NAV per switch; gross AND net; matched-exposure
random-timing placebo (3,000 draws).

| window | strategy | net total | net CAGR | net Sharpe | exposure |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2019-03 → 2026-06** | S2F residual timer | **+328%** | +22.1% | 0.71 | 59% |
| | buy-and-hold | **+1355%** | +44.5% | **0.91** | 100% |
| | random-timing placebo | mean +87% (p95 **+409%**) | | | 59% |
| **2021-11 → 2026-06** | S2F residual timer | +7% | +1.4% | 0.25 | 78% |
| | buy-and-hold | −4% | −0.9% | 0.24 | 100% |
| | random-timing placebo | mean −39% (p95 +17%) | | | 78% |

Gross ≈ net (only 9 switches over seven years). The timer **loses to buy-and-hold on both total
return and Sharpe** out-of-sample, and its +328% sits *below* the 95th percentile of a
matched-exposure random calendar (+409%) — indistinguishable from spending the same fraction of
days long at random. In the post-2021 "broke" window it is a wash (+7% vs −4%): once the model
line explodes past the price, the rule reads "always cheap, always long" ≈ buy-and-hold.

## 5 · Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic world with an exogenous, stationary valuation gap and an explicitly-planted
mean-reversion coefficient `beta`; the detector regresses forward returns on the gap. No network.

| world | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (beta = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.17** (sd 1.29), \|t\| ≥ 2 in 5/20 |
| planted (beta = 0.03, seed 765) | **−5.96** |

The detector recovers a real planted effect cleanly and is unbiased under the null (centred at
zero). The null's wide spread — 5/20 seeds crossing |t| ≥ 2 on overlapping windows with a
persistent regressor — is itself the study's lesson in miniature: heavy autocorrelation and
non-stationarity inflate apparent significance, which is exactly why the out-of-sample |t| < 2 is
the honest bar. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Out-of-sample, the valuation residual predicts forward BTC returns at no
  horizon with |t| ≥ 2 (best −1.68, 180d). The full-sample "significance" is the fit talking to
  itself. The famous R² ≈ 0.9 is a spurious regression: `ln(SF)` is 96% correlated with calendar
  time and a plain price-on-time trend fits equally well (0.876 vs 0.880).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A buy-when-cheap-vs-model timer returns +328% net vs buy-and-hold's
  +1355% out-of-sample (and loses on Sharpe, 0.71 vs 0.91), landing below the 95th percentile of
  a random-timing placebo. Post-2021 it collapses to buy-and-hold. There is no edge to capture.
- **Model holds out-of-sample? — BUSTED.** Coefficients frozen at publication: R² falls from
  0.705 to 0.213; the model implied a six-figure BTC floor through the 2022 crash to $17k and
  stands ~4× above the realised tape ($247k vs $59k) by 2026. A beautiful in-sample curve fit to
  a clock, that knew nothing about the future.
